title: Influence of Mid-infrared Galactic Bubble on Surroundings: A Case Study on IRAS 16489-4431
question: What is the influence of a massive star on a mid-infrared bubble and its surrounding gas in IRAS 16489-4431?

data.sensitivity: rms 0.2 mJy/beam (continuum), 6.4 mJy/beam per 0.122 MHz channel (H13CO+)

what.value: Herschel PPMAP dust temperature map (~12'' resolution)

evidence.quote: The final resolution of the temperature map is $\sim$12$''$.
having an angular radius of 0.2$'$ (cite: jayasinghe2019)
The corresponding bolometric luminosities of 2690 and 3900 L$_\odot$ are adopted from (cite: lang1999).

what.value: Wind velocity ~700 km/s and mass-loss rate ~10^-9.4 Msun/yr for B1V star

evidence.quote: $V\sim$700 km s$^{-1}$ and $\dot{\mathrm{M}}$ of $\sim$10$^{-9.4}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ for a typical B1V star were obtained from (cite: oskinova2011).

recipe.method: Dendrogram on ALMA 3 mm continuum; leaves with area >33 pixels and S/N>5 are cores; parameters refined with CASA imfit
Optically thin dust mass equation of Hildebrand 1983
assumptions: gas-to-dust ratio 100; kappa = 10 (nu/1.2 THz)^beta; distance 3.26 kpc

recipe.goal: fit SED of the influencing source to get mass
recipe.method: Robitaille et al. 2007 SED fitter with distance 3.0-3.6 kpc and Av 3-30; models with chi2-chi2best<=3 used

answer_key.quantity: Mass of core C3 (beta=1.5, T=21 K)

evidence.quote: The estimated mass of 7.9$\pm$0.7 M$_{\odot}$ is referring to a B2-B1 type star.
We found a total of 8 Class I and 5 Class II sources within the targeted regions.

not_stated_but_needed: Calibration, CASA version and imaging parameters (robust, cleaning) of the ATOMS data
H13CO+ moment/integration velocity range and rest frequency

score_reason: Simple analysis with public data and a few stated parameters, but imaging details are deferred to another paper.
